To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neuregulin signaling is important for maintaining auditory sensitivity in the mature gunea pig cochlea.
chronic local application of neureguline receptor blockers leads to a progressive loss of hearing despite normal hair cell function and a preserved number of auditory neurons.

chronic local application of a substance that blocks neuregulin signaling leads to progressive hearing impairment, and that this impairment is due to alterations in the function of the auditory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of hearing loss.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control hearing in the mammalian inner ear.

the mechanisms that control the survival and maintenance of auditory neurons in the mature cochlear nucleus, the role of neuregulns in this process and the consequences of neureglin/erbB signaling block for hearing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuregulin‐1 and neuregulin 4, and their receptors, erbB2 and erbB3, are essential for long‐term maintenance of hearing sensitivity in the guinea pig.
neuregulin signaling plays a role in maintaining the sensitivity and responsiveness of the auditory neurons in the mature cochlear system.
neuregulin receptor block leads to progressive hearing loss, which is not due to loss of hair cells or spiral ganglion neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
erbB signaling is critical for maintaining cochlear sensitivity.
neuregulin‐1/erbB signaling is critical to maintaining the sensitivity of the cochlea, but not its structural integrity.
neuregulin signaling is critical for the maintenance of hearing function in the mature cochlear organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that

neuregulin‐1 signaling plays an important role in maintaining the functional integrity of the mature cochlea, and that the loss of this function leads to a progressive and irreversible loss of cochlear sensitivity.
neuregulin receptor block leads to progressive hearing impairment that is not caused by hair cell damage or loss, but rather is due to a loss of auditory nerve excitability.
neuregulin signaling is important not only during development but also in maintaining the functional state of the auditory system throughout life.
